topic.title: Release notes for 0.3
topic.shortdesc: Release lines per minor version, a version picker that follows them, site settings declared in the docs repository, and context help that follows the field, button or pane in use and answers public apps without a token.

ul.li: Release lines by minor version: a repository can keep one live release per minor (0.22, 0.23) instead of per major, so each reader keeps the docs of their own minor. Switch it under Site & access → Release lines in the admin console. Repositories stay on major lines until staff switch. See .

The version picker has a new mode, Every live version (live), which offers every live line, newest first, with no list to keep. The public release version can be latest, the newest live line. Both follow publishing and retiring by themselves. A list offers only versions that have a live release. See .
New admin API route PUT /admin/api/repos/:id/release-lines, a releaseLines field on POST /admin/api/repos and in seed files, and the repo.release-lines audit action.

section.title: Site settings in the docs repository

ul.li: A site block in opend.config.yaml declares release refs, release lines, access, public entitlements and the version picker. The build that goes live on the newest release line applies it, and the declared settings are read-only in the console. See .
A site with no docs source connects by itself to the one repository its GitHub App can access, when that repository has an opend.config.yaml.
The admin API answers 409 for a setting the repository declares, and seeds leave declared settings alone. New audit action repo.release-refs.

Help for the field, button or pane in use: context help can follow what the reader is doing, not just the page. It tries the field with focus, then the button pressed last, then the tab or pane, then the view. Mark them with data-help-key and data-help-pane, or report them with OpenDHelp.setActivity. The help JSON API and context links take focus, action and pane parameters, and the API's answer says which signal it used. See .

On a public site, the help JSON API answers without a token: exactly what an anonymous visitor sees, even with embedding off, so no secret goes into your app. Every answer names its release in OpenD-Release and OpenD-Release-Line. See .
GET /api/v1/help/nav: the reader's navigation, for apps that draw a help sidebar.
Context links for public sites, /context/app/key, redirect to the help topic. See .
The previewer's help lab tries a focused field, last pressed button and pane as well as a path. See .
A Custom domain page, where staff of a managed site set, change or remove its domain and see the DNS records to add and whether they are in place. See .
The Release lines form and the new version picker choices described above.
GET /api/v1/nav no longer lists the navtitle of a topic that the key's audience cannot see.
Managed sites rebuild on pushes from a GitHub App created in their admin console. Before, those pushes were refused.
The version menu's label keeps full contrast in every theme.

The help widget works in host apps whose Content Security Policy allows no inline styles (style-src 'self'): it styles its button and panel with constructable stylesheets. Before, the panel was blocked from being styled there. See .
New command opend package writes one reader's docs as a static site that opens offline, as a zip file or a folder, optionally with their PDFs. Only what that reader may see goes in. See .

section.title: Upgrading from 0.2
section.p: Deploy the new image. Migrations 012_release_lines and 013_declared_site_settings are applied on start. Repositories keep major release lines and their stored settings, so readers see no change until staff switch lines or the repository declares a site block.
The new environment variables are optional: OPEND_HOSTING_URL and OPEND_HOSTING_TOKEN are set by a hosting provider, and OPEND_FLEET_REDIRECTS applies only to a multi-site fleet. See and .
